key_cases.case_name: People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals, Inc. v. Department of Agricultural Resources
key_cases.holding: The SJC construed the public safety and privacy exemptions to the public records law, holding that the statutes favor disclosure by presuming records are public and placing on the custodian the burden of proving with specificity that an exemption applies.
key_cases.relevance: Systematic data collection from Massachusetts agencies operates within the presumption and exemption scheme PETA describes.
key_cases.quote: Together, these statutes, and our cases interpreting them, favor disclosure of public records in two primary ways.

key_cases.case_name: United States Department of Justice v. Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court reversed, holding that FOIA Exemption 7(C) categorically protects an FBI criminal-history "rap sheet" from disclosure to a third-party requester, because the privacy interest in the practical obscurity of compiled information outweighs a public interest that FOIA measures only by what the record would reveal about the government's own conduct.
key_cases.relevance: Reporters Committee holds that aggregating individually obtainable records into a compilation creates a privacy interest of its own, the central legal constraint on systematic data collection across agency records.
key_cases.quote: Official information that sheds light on an agency's performance of its statutory duties falls squarely within that statutory purpose.
